text: Team-member effectiveness frameworks emphasize clear contribution expectations: knowing who owns which tasks, what 'done' means, and how progress will be checked. Role ambiguity often shows up as duplicated work, dropped tasks, or disagreement about responsibilities rather than as proof of bad intent.
limitations: Does not establish individual motivation
Requires team participation to fully resolve

text: Accountability interventions that help student teams include agreeing on task ownership, setting visible checkpoints, and giving behavior-specific feedback about missed commitments. Focus on observable work patterns (what was promised, what was delivered, when) rather than labeling a teammate as lazy or uncaring.
limitations: Uneven contribution may also reflect skill, access, confidence, or capacity
Workplace studies may not fully transfer to short academic projects

text: Psychological safety describes a climate where people can ask questions, admit mistakes, and offer ideas without fear of embarrassment or punishment. Low psychological safety often appears as silence in meetings, withheld concerns, or idea dismissal. Useful next steps include inviting input explicitly, responding non-defensively to concerns, and separating idea critique from personal criticism.
limitations: Classic evidence is often workplace rather than student-team context
Silence does not automatically mean agreement or disengagement

text: Intragroup conflict research distinguishes task conflict (disagreement about the work content), process conflict (how work should be done), and relationship/interpersonal conflict. Treating every disagreement as a personality clash can escalate issues. For process conflict, clarifying roles, decision rules, and timelines is often more useful than debating motives.
limitations: Conflict type alone does not identify root causes
Brief reflections cannot fully diagnose hidden causes

text: Uneven work distribution is a common student-team complaint. Practical options include making a shared task board, assigning owners for each deliverable, setting interim checkpoints before the final deadline, and discussing capacity constraints early. Avoid assuming the quieter teammate is uncommitted; skill gaps, unclear roles, or competing deadlines can produce the same pattern.
limitations: Does not establish individual motivation
May not apply to very short one-week assignments

text: Behavior-specific feedback is usually more usable than character judgments. A practical pattern is: describe the observable behavior, note the impact on the team deliverable, and request a concrete next step. Example: 'The CAD draft was due Friday and I did not see an upload; that blocked the simulation. Can we set a midpoint check on Wednesday?'
limitations: Qualitative practical guidance rather than causal evidence
Requires psychological safety to land well

text: Unequal voice can appear when one or two members dominate discussion, ideas are dismissed quickly, or some members are rarely invited to contribute. Inclusive practices include rotating facilitation, explicitly inviting quieter members, capturing all options before deciding, and checking that decisions are not finalized in side channels.
limitations: Does not determine whether bias occurred
Formal discrimination concerns require human/university pathways

text: A lightweight team charter or norms document can reduce later conflict by clarifying meeting expectations, communication channels, decision rules, quality standards, and what to do when someone will miss a deadline. Charters work best when revisited after early milestones rather than created once and ignored.
limitations: Requires team participation
May not help if immediate safety or misconduct issues are present

text: Decision process conflicts often look like last-minute choices, decisions made without input, or repeated reopening of settled issues. Helpful practices include naming the decision owner, listing options, setting a decide-by date, and recording the rationale in a shared note so the team can move forward.
limitations: Does not resolve deep interpersonal harm
Time pressure may constrain ideal process

text: Diagnostic caution: a short student reflection is not a complete account of team dynamics. Visible conflict, conflict sources, and underlying issues are not the same. Coaching should treat possible causes as hypotheses, avoid motive claims, and recommend proportionate next steps while noting when instructor or university support is more appropriate.
limitations: Not a substitute for formal investigation or counseling
Cannot infer hidden motives from brief text
